channel.title: Come, Follow, Lead
channel.description: A daily leadership commentary on the Come Follow Me reading -- for a soldier, an electrician, a business owner, and a dad raising two boys toward Christ.
channel.itunes:author: Come, Follow, Lead

item.title: Thursday: "He Hath Borne Our Griefs, and Carried Our Sorrows" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 54; 57:15–19 -- Jesus Christ wants me to return to Him; reassurance of God's everlasting kindness

item.title: Tuesday: "He Hath Borne Our Griefs, and Carried Our Sorrows" (day 2 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 52 -- The Lord's people are called to awake and put on strength; good tidings of deliverance

item.title: Sunday Review: "Comfort Ye My People"
item.description: A full recap of the week's reading -- Isaiah 40–49 -- to get you ready for church.

item.title: Saturday: "Comfort Ye My People" (day 6 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 49 -- The Lord's servant is prepared even before birth for a mission to Israel and the Gentiles as 'a light' to them. Though efforts may seem 'for nought, and in vain' (49:4), the Lord assures His people He can never forget them, comparing His remembrance to a mother who cannot forget her nursing child.

item.title: Friday: "Comfort Ye My People" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 48 -- The Lord recounts His foreknowledge and His refining of Israel 'in the furnace of affliction' (48:10), and pleads for obedience, promising that peace would have flowed 'as a river' and righteousness 'as the waves of the sea' if they had hearkened to His commandments.

item.title: Thursday: "Comfort Ye My People" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 46–47 -- Contrast between the false gods of Babylon (carried as burdens) and the true God who carries His people 'even to your old age' (46:4). Chapter 47 is a direct pronouncement of judgment against Babylon, Israel's captor, reminding them that worldly power will fall.

item.title: Wednesday: "Comfort Ye My People" (day 3 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 44–45 -- The Lord pours out His Spirit like water on dry ground, denounces idol worship, and declares Himself the only God ('I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God,' 44:6). Cyrus is named as the Lord's shepherd/anointed who will allow the Jews to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple.

item.title: Tuesday: "Comfort Ye My People" (day 2 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 42–43 -- The Lord's chosen servant is introduced (identified with Jesus Christ), bringing judgment and light to the Gentiles, opening blind eyes. Chapter 43 delivers the powerful message 'Fear not... I have redeemed thee' and Israel's role as the Lord's witnesses, that 'beside me there is no saviour' (43:11).

item.title: Monday: "Comfort Ye My People" (day 1 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 40–41 -- The Lord's comfort and power begin here: 'Comfort ye my people' opens a new tone in Isaiah's prophecies. Chapter 40 speaks of preparing 'the way of the Lord,' God's incomparable greatness compared to nations and idols, and the promise that those who wait on the Lord 'shall renew their strength ... mount up with wings as eagles' (40:31). Chapter 41 continues with the Lord's reassurance to Israel, 'Fear thou not; for I am with thee' (41:10), and His call of His servant.

item.title: Sunday Review: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder"
item.description: A full recap of the week's reading -- Isaiah 13–14; 22; 24–30; 35 -- to get you ready for church.

item.title: Saturday: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder" (day 6 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 30:18–26; 35 -- The Lord's mercy and healing power; the parched ground becoming a pool—hope of restoration and renewal for God's people.

item.title: Friday: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 29 -- The Lord can restore what is lost or broken; Isaiah 29 contains parallels to the Restoration, including the coming forth of the Book of Mormon and the First Vision.

item.title: Thursday: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 29:7–13; 30:8–14 -- Further warnings on turning away from the Lord—comparisons to hunger and thirst, and a broken wall or vessel.

item.title: Wednesday: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder" (day 3 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 24:1–12; 28:1–8 -- Turning away from the Lord brings spiritual danger—spiritual warning signs, comparisons to a sad empty earth and drunkenness.

item.title: Tuesday: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder" (day 2 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 22; 24:21–23; 25:6–8; 26:19; 28:16 -- Jesus Christ is the promised Messiah—His atoning sacrifice, Resurrection, and Second Coming; 'He will swallow up death in victory.'

item.title: Monday: "A Marvellous Work and a Wonder" (day 1 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 13–14 -- Isaiah's warning against Babylon, symbolizing pride, greed, and sin; comparison of the Babylonian king's pride to Satan's pride; the Savior gives rest from sorrow and fear.

item.title: Sunday Review: "God Is My Salvation"
item.description: A full recap of the week's reading -- Isaiah 1–12 -- to get you ready for church.

item.title: Saturday: "God Is My Salvation" (day 6 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 10–12 -- Continuation of God's great latter-day work: judgment on Assyria, the stem of Jesse, the ensign to the nations, and songs of praise and salvation.

item.title: Friday: "God Is My Salvation" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 7–9 -- God promised to send Jesus Christ to be my Savior. Isaiah counsels Ahaz to trust the Lord amid the Syria-Israel alliance, and gives well-known Messianic prophecies (Immanuel, Wonderful Counsellor, Prince of Peace).

item.title: Thursday: "God Is My Salvation" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 6 -- Prophets are called by God. Isaiah recounts his call to be a prophet.

item.title: Wednesday: "God Is My Salvation" (day 3 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 3–5 -- Continued warnings about the people's spiritual condition (daughters of Zion, the vineyard parable) alongside promises of hope and the branch of Jesse.

item.title: Tuesday: "God Is My Salvation" (day 2 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 2 -- God will do a great work in the latter days. Isaiah 2:2–4 speaks of the mountain of the Lord's house, temples, and the gathering of nations to learn His ways.

item.title: Monday: "God Is My Salvation" (day 1 of 6)
item.description: Isaiah 1 -- Prophets warn about sin and promise hope through repentance. Look for phrases describing the people's spiritual condition and the consequences of it, as well as messages of hope and redemption through the Savior.

item.title: Sunday Review: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths"
item.description: A full recap of the week's reading -- Proverbs 1-4; 15-16; 22; 31; Ecclesiastes 1-3; 11-12 -- to get you ready for church.

item.title: Saturday: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths" (day 6 of 6)
item.description: Ecclesiastes 11-12 -- The conclusion of the matter: fear God and keep His commandments; finding eternal value and meaning in life.

item.title: Friday: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Ecclesiastes 1-3 -- The Preacher's reflections on the vanity and temporary nature of mortal life, and the search for meaning.

item.title: Thursday: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Proverbs 22; 31 -- The virtuous woman of great spiritual strength and influence described in Proverbs 31, alongside wisdom themes from chapter 22.

item.title: Wednesday: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths" (day 3 of 6)
item.description: Proverbs 15-16 -- A soft answer turns away wrath; using kind words and Christlike communication, including in modern digital contexts.

item.title: Tuesday: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths" (day 2 of 6)
item.description: Proverbs 3-4 -- Trusting in the Lord with all your heart rather than leaning on your own understanding; letting the Lord direct your paths.

item.title: Monday: "He Shall Direct Thy Paths" (day 1 of 6)
item.description: Proverbs 1-2 -- The purpose of Proverbs as wise counsel; the call to incline your ear to wisdom and the value of seeking knowledge and understanding.

item.title: Sunday Review: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord"
item.description: A full recap of the week's reading -- Psalms 102–103; 110; 116–119; 127–128; 135–139; 146–150 -- to get you ready for church.

item.title: Saturday: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord" (day 6 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 146–150 -- 'Praise ye the Lord.' The final psalms are a call to praise, considering reasons and ways to praise God.

item.title: Friday: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 137–139 -- The Lord knows my heart. Psalm 139 emphasizes that God is fully aware of our thoughts, actions, strengths, and weaknesses.

item.title: Thursday: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 127–128; 134–136 -- The Lord is more powerful than any idol. Psalms 134–36 list the powerful things the Lord has done, contrasting with the foolishness of trusting false gods (135:15–18).

item.title: Wednesday: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord" (day 3 of 6)
item.description: Psalm 119 -- God's word will keep me on His path. Psalm 119 uses journey imagery—'walk,' 'path,' 'way,' 'feet,' 'wander'—to describe our path back to Heavenly Father.

item.title: Tuesday: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord" (day 2 of 6)
item.description: Psalm 116; Psalms 110; 118 -- Continuing the theme of calling on the Lord in trials (Psalm 116), then turning to how Jesus Christ fulfilled prophecies from the Psalms in Psalms 110 and 118.

item.title: Monday: "Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise the Lord" (day 1 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 102–103 -- The Lord can comfort me in my suffering. Psalm 102:1–11 describes anxiety and isolation in trials; 102:12–28 and 103 shift to praise and confidence in God's mercy.

item.title: Sunday Review: "I Will Declare What He Hath Done for My Soul"
item.description: A full recap of the week's reading -- Psalms 49–51; 61–66; 69–72; 77–78; 85–86 -- to get you ready for church.

item.title: Saturday: "I Will Declare What He Hath Done for My Soul" (day 6 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 64–66; 85–86 -- Declaring what God has done for my soul; God hears and answers prayer; His mercy and willingness to forgive

item.title: Friday: "I Will Declare What He Hath Done for My Soul" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 77–78 -- Remembering the works of the Lord and His wonders of old to set our hope in God

item.title: Friday: "I Will Declare What He Hath Done for My Soul" (day 5 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 77–78 -- Remembering the works of the Lord and His wonders of old to set our hope in God

item.title: Thursday: "I Will Declare What He Hath Done for My Soul" (day 4 of 6)
item.description: Psalms 70–72 -- Testimony of Jesus Christ can help others come unto Him; telling others about Christ
